what: The heuristic reconstructs the complete directed routing-cost matrix once in new() from grounded visit and return-to-depot operators using metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. It identifies customer visited facts, all location facts, and the depot from semantic fact names rather than variable IDs. Exact-name numeric lookup optionally recovers capacity, load, and per-customer demands; if any are unavailable, routing estimation remains active without capacity reasoning. At evaluation time it finds the current location and unvisited customers, computes an MST connectivity estimate over the current location, depot, and remaining customers, and performs a nearest-neighbour completion rollout. When resource data is available, the rollout respects residual vehicle capacity and inserts depot restarts when necessary. The returned value is the maximum of the MST and a blend weighted toward the rollout. Reusable RefCell scratch storage limits repeated allocation.
why: CVRP states are principally distinguished by the remaining customer set, current endpoint, and residual route capacity. A plain unsatisfied-goal count ignores the large geometric differences visible in these instances, while an MST captures global routing structure cheaply in quadratic time. The nearest-neighbour rollout adds endpoint sensitivity and approximates a complete remaining solution, including the multiple depot trips that dominate low-capacity instances. Blending it with the more stable MST moderates greedy-rollout error while retaining strong search guidance. Grounded operator costs are used because they are reliable even when the translator folds away travel-cost, capacity, or demand fluents; optional exact-name resource recovery improves estimates when those fluents survive translation without making the heuristic instance-dependent or fragile.
